# Security Review: `portal/portal_payment.php` **Recommendation: do not merge.** The change adds a new card-data exposure path (`recid`) and leaks gateway credentials. It also builds on existing access-control and PCI flaws that this page relies on and that remain unfixed. --- ## Critical ### 1. IDOR via the new `recid` parameter exposes decrypted card data - **Location:** `$recid = (int) $_REQUEST['recid']` → `$appsql->getPortalAuditRec($recid)` → `json_decode(decryptStandard($edata['checksum']))` - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control - **Problem:** Any portal patient can supply any `recid`. Nothing checks that the audit record belongs to `$_SESSION['pid']`. The record's encrypted card blob is decrypted and rendered in the payment panel. - The change also adds `|| isset($ccdata["transId"])` to the unmasking condition, so the **full card number** is shown to non-staff for processed records. - For other records, the CVV (`cardCode`) and expiry are printed, regardless of user type. - **Impact:** A patient can enumerate `recid` values and harvest other patients' names, ZIP codes, full card numbers, expiry dates and CVVs. - **Fix:** - For portal sessions, ignore `recid`, or verify `audit.patient_id == $_SESSION['pid']`. - Never unmask the PAN based on `transId`. ### 2. Portal patients can override `pid` and view or post for any patient (pre-existing, relied upon) - **Location:** - `$pid = isset($_REQUEST['pid']) ? $_REQUEST['pid'] : $pid;` - `$pid = $_REQUEST['hidden_patient_code'] > 0 ? ...` - `$form_pid = $_POST['form_pid']` - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control - **Problem:** The session `pid` is replaced by request input even when `$isPortal` is true. A patient can view another patient's demographics, insurance copay, encounters, balances and card audit data by changing `pid`. The new `$isPortal` flag is set but never used to stop this. - **Fix:** When `$isPortal`, force `$pid = $form_pid = $_SESSION['pid']` and reject any mismatch. ### 3. Portal patients can directly invoke the staff "Post Payment" logic (pre-existing) - **Location:** `if ($_POST['form_save']) { ... }` - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control / A04 Insecure Design - **Problem:** The save block is only hidden in the UI (the button renders only when `authUserID` is set). There is no server-side check. A portal user can POST `form_save` with: - `radio_type_of_payment=cash`, which runs `UPDATE billing SET billed=1` and `UPDATE form_encounter SET last_level_closed=4`; - or `pre_payment` / `invoice_balance`, which insert `ar_session` / `ar_activity` / `payments` rows. This lets a patient record fake payments and close out balances without paying, for any `form_pid` (see #2). - **Fix:** Wrap the whole block in `if (!$isPortal && isset($_SESSION['authUserID']) && AclMain::aclCheckCore('acct','bill'))`. ### 4. Gateway secret leaked to the browser - **Location:** `var apiKey = ;` - **Category:** A02 Cryptographic Failures / A05 Security Misconfiguration - **Problem:** This line is emitted for every gateway and every viewer. In OpenEMR, `gateway_api_key` is the "API Login / **Secret**" setting. - For Stripe it holds the **secret key**, giving full account control: charges, refunds and customer data. - For Authorize.Net the API Login ID is needed client-side. It is still unnecessary for the other gateways. - The global is an encrypted setting, so the raw ciphertext may also be leaked. - **Fix:** - Only output `gateway_public_key` (plus the Authorize.Net login ID when that gateway is active, after decryption). - Never send the Stripe secret to the client. - Rotate the key if this has been deployed. --- ## High ### 5. Storing and displaying full PAN and CVV (InHouse mode; pre-existing, extended) - **Location:** - The `paySubmit` flow posts `cardNumber`, `cardCode`, `month` and `year` to `paylib.php`, where they are stored encrypted in `onsite_portal_activity.checksum`. - The display code echoes `cardNumber` and `cardCode`. - **Category:** A02 Cryptographic Failures / A04 Insecure Design - **Problem:** PCI DSS forbids storing CVV/CVC after authorization in any form, and limits PAN display to those with a business need. Staff, and now patients via #1, see the full PAN and CVV. Encryption with an application-wide key that the web app decrypts on view gives little protection. - **Fix:** - Remove or disable InHouse card capture in favour of tokenizing gateways. - Never persist `cardCode`. - Mask the PAN to the last 4 digits for all users. ### 6. Stored XSS through an unescaped card number - **Location:** `echo $ccdata["cardNumber"] . "
";` - **Category:** A03 Injection (XSS) - **Problem:** `cardNumber` is attacker-controlled patient input (client-side `pattern` / `maxlength` are trivially bypassed). It is echoed raw on the staff audit view, and via #1 to other patients. A payload like `` runs in a billing user's session, enabling account takeover and further fraudulent posting. - **Fix:** Use `text()` (as is done for every neighbouring field) and validate server-side that the value is digits only. ### 7. No CSRF protection on financial state changes (pre-existing) - **Location:** The `invoiceForm` POST to `portal_payment.php` and the `paylib.php` submissions. - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control (CSRF) - **Problem:** No CSRF token is generated or checked. A malicious page can make a logged-in staff member's browser post payments, mark encounters billed and close them. - **Fix:** Add `CsrfUtils::collectCsrfToken()` hidden fields and call `CsrfUtils::verifyCsrfToken()` before any write. --- ## Medium ### 8. No server-side validation of payment amounts - **Location:** `$_REQUEST['form_prepayment']` and `$_POST['form_upay'][...]` - **Category:** A04 Insecure Design - **Problem:** The "Negative payments not accepted" check is JavaScript only. Negative, non-numeric or enormous amounts are written straight into `ar_session.pay_total`, `ar_activity.pay_amount` and `payments`. Combined with #3, this allows ledger manipulation. - **Fix:** Validate server-side that amounts are positive decimals with 2 decimal places, within the invoice balance. ### 9. Receipt path trusts request input - **Location:** `if ($_POST['form_save'] || $_REQUEST['receipt'])`, which uses `$form_pid` / `$payrow` from the request. - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control - **Problem:** A portal user can request receipts for other patients' payments. - **Fix:** Bind the receipt lookup to the session `pid` for portal users. ### 10. Missing or incorrect audit attribution for postings - **Location:** - `user_id = $_SESSION['authUserID']` and `post_user = $_SESSION['authUserID']` (null for portal sessions). - `$_SESSION['authId']` is used inconsistently in the copay branch. - **Category:** A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures - **Problem:** Payments posted through the portal path (#3) are recorded with no user. Fraudulent entries cannot be traced. Patient-side posting attempts are not logged as security events. - **Fix:** - Block portal posting. - Always record an actor. - Log denied attempts via `EventAuditLogger`. --- ## Low ### 11. Output-encoding inconsistencies - **Category:** A03 Injection - **Problems:** - `xlt('Invoice')` is used inside a `value='...'` attribute; it should be `xla`. - `xlt(...)` is used inside a JS `prompt("...")` string; it should be `xlj` or `json_encode`. - `addslashes(xl(...))` is used in JS strings. - `$GLOBALS['webroot']` and `$GLOBALS['assets_static_relative']` are echoed unescaped into URLs and JS. - **Impact:** These are admin- or translation-controlled, so low risk, but they should be fixed with the correct helpers (`attr`, `js_escape`). ### 12. Dead `$isPortal` flag and UI-only gating - **Category:** A04 Insecure Design - **Problem:** The PR introduces `$isPortal` but relies on the CSS `hidden` class and conditional button rendering to separate patient and staff capabilities. This gives a false sense of protection; see #2 and #3. ### 13. Outdated or unpinned client components - **Category:** A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components - **Problem:** `jquery-creditcardvalidator` is legacy. The new Accept.js / Stripe.js code depends on externally loaded scripts whose inclusion and integrity (SRI or CSP) are not visible here. - **Fix:** Confirm they load from official HTTPS endpoints under a CSP. --- ## Summary | # | Issue | OWASP | Severity | |---|-------|-------|----------| | 1 | `recid` IDOR, full PAN/CVV disclosure | A01 | Critical | | 2 | `pid` override by portal user | A01 | Critical | | 3 | Portal user can post payments / close billing | A01/A04 | Critical | | 4 | `gateway_api_key` (Stripe secret) sent to browser | A02/A05 | Critical | | 5 | PAN + CVV storage and display | A02/A04 | High | | 6 | Stored XSS via `cardNumber` | A03 | High | | 7 | No CSRF on financial writes | A01 | High | | 8 | No server-side amount validation | A04 | Medium | | 9 | Receipt IDOR | A01 | Medium | | 10 | Missing actor in payment audit trail | A09 | Medium | | 11 | Encoding inconsistencies | A03 | Low | | 12 | UI-only privilege separation | A04 | Low | | 13 | Legacy / unverified JS components | A06 | Low |
